interest: This file provides a fascinating and rare glimpse into the legal and administrative handling of personal property left behind by interned Japanese diplomats and prominent nationals undergoing repatriation in the early months of World War II. It shows high-level coordination among notable figures—including FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover, Librarian of Congress Archibald MacLeish, and Assistant Secretaries of State Adolf A. Berle, Jr. and G. Howland Shaw—over a single scholarly work belonging to Tamon Maeda (former Director of the Japanese Institute in New York City and later Japan's postwar Minister of Education). Crucially, rather than declaring the book seized enemy property under the Alien Property Custodian, State Department officials deliberately structured the transfer to the Library of Congress as an 'indefinite loan' for safe-keeping, specifically anticipating and respecting Maeda's postwar property rights to avoid future diplomatic embarrassment.
overview: This file documents the discovery, evaluation, and inter-agency disposition of a Japanese-language reference book—a chronological table of Japanese literature—left at the Greenbrier Hotel in White Sulphur Springs, West Virginia, by Tamon Mayeda, former Director of the Japanese Institute in New York City, while interned there with other Japanese diplomats awaiting repatriation in 1942. Transmitted to Assistant Secretary of State Adolf A. Berle, Jr. by FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover, the scholarly volume was reviewed by the State Department's Division of Far Eastern Affairs and Special Division. To avoid complications with enemy property custodianship and ensure the book could be returned to Maeda without embarrassment after the war, the Department arranged to deposit the book with the Library of Congress on an indefinite loan for safe-keeping, which the Library formally acknowledged in September 1942.

subfiles.about: Recommendation by the Division of Far Eastern Affairs to forward a Japanese literature book left by an interned Japanese national to the Library of Congress.
subfiles.summary: This internal State Department memorandum discusses a Japanese chronological table of literature transmitted by FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover. The Division of Far Eastern Affairs recommends that the volume be transferred to the Library of Congress, where it would be of greater value than to the Department. The memo notes the book was left at the Greenbrier Hotel by an interned Japanese national and consults the Special Division regarding whether it should instead be treated as enemy property or delivered to representatives of Japanese interests.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum on Disposition of Japanese Literature Book

subfiles.about: Recommendation by the Special Division that the book be transferred to the Library of Congress as an indefinite loan to preserve the owner's property rights.
subfiles.summary: Joseph C. Green of the State Department's Special Division responds to Maxwell M. Hamilton, agreeing to send the Japanese literature book to the Library of Congress. Green stipulates that the cover letter to Archibald MacLeish must state the volume is on indefinite loan from the Department. This proviso was designed to ensure the book could be returned without diplomatic embarrassment to its rightful owner, Tamon Mayeda, should he claim it after the war.
subfiles.title: Special Division Memorandum Concerning Indefinite Loan of Book to Library of Congress
subfiles.to: Maxwell M. Hamilton (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)

subfiles.about: Official deposit receipt from the Library of Congress acknowledging receipt of the Japanese literature volume for safe-keeping.
subfiles.from: John H. Moriarty (Chief, Division of Accessions, Library of Congress) for Archibald MacLeish
subfiles.summary: The Library of Congress issues formal deposit receipt No. 724 to Assistant Secretary of State G. Howland Shaw. Signed by John H. Moriarty on behalf of Librarian Archibald MacLeish, the document acknowledges receipt of the chronological table of Japanese literature. It formally certifies that the volume will be held on deposit for safe-keeping, subject to withdrawal by the State Department at any time.
subfiles.title: Library of Congress Deposit Receipt for Japanese Chronological Table
subfiles.to: G. Howland Shaw (Assistant Secretary of State)

subfiles.about: Transmittal letter from FBI Director Hoover forwarding the Japanese reference book found at the Greenbrier Hotel to Assistant Secretary Berle.
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover (Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation)
subfiles.summary: FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover transmits to Assistant Secretary of State Adolf A. Berle, Jr. a chronological table of Japanese literature left at the Greenbrier Hotel in White Sulphur Springs, West Virginia. The book belonged to Tamon Mayeda, former Director of the Japanese Institute in New York City, who had been detained with other Japanese diplomats awaiting repatriation. Hoover describes the book as a scholarly work indexing Japanese authors, their writings, and concurrent world historical events, and suggests forwarding it to the Japanese Department of the Library of Congress if not needed by the State Department.
subfiles.title: Letter from FBI Director Hoover to Assistant Secretary Berle Transmitting Japanese Book
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle, Jr. (Assistant Secretary of State)

subfiles.about: Official State Department letter transferring the Japanese chronological table to Librarian of Congress Archibald MacLeish on indefinite loan.
subfiles.from: G. Howland Shaw (Assistant Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary of State G. Howland Shaw writes to Librarian of Congress Archibald MacLeish transmitting the chronological table of Japanese literature received from the FBI. Shaw notes that the Library may find the book of interest for reference purposes and states that the Department of State is pleased to provide it on indefinite loan. The document is accompanied by a true copy attestation signed by W. H. Hiller.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Archibald MacLeish Loaning Japanese Book
